newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on Ahold results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Ahold results.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Koninklijke Ahold NV said on Wednesday third quarter net profit rose to 156.4 million guilders from 101.6 million a year ago.
Lidy Knigge, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett:

"At first sight they look like very decent numbers. The operating result in the U.S. has been depressed by some non-recurring costs. That explains why the total operating result came in below my expectations. But the operating result in the Netherlands and Rest of Europe was in line. Sales in the U.S. were slightly higher than expected.

"They were over $3 billion when we were going for $2.8 billion. But we have only consolidated Stop and Shop from August 1 and the company has consolidated it from July 22. But that only party explains it. There's a slightly positive surprise there. Net profit and EPS were in line (with our forecasts). We were quite satisifed but (they're) nothing spectacular."

"What I see is that it was below my expectations of 168 million net, but it's nothing serious that I can see right now, because a few positive trends like sales per store figures in the U.S. are good.

"The operating margin in the U.S. was slightly below my expectations but there was a mixed effect from Stop and Shop. I was counting on an average operating of 3.25 percent and it turned out to be 3.1 percent. Identical sales growth was looking very good for Bi-Lo, it was in trouble in 1995. The last two quarters we saw recovery and it's very strong this time -- 4.2 percent identical sales growth. The losses in the start-up operation in the Far East was two million more than I expected. The interest on capital leases was a little bit higher than I expected and on an operating level it was just the U.S. that was a little bit less than I expected.
"As I see it now there are no real problems, I'm not disappointed because it's a good spread of profits."

"Broadly speaking, the results were nice and roughly as we expected. The charges of $12 million taken in the U.S. came as a surprise to me and the start-up costs (6.8 million guilders) in Asia were slightly higher than I had expected. On balance earnings were in line with our expectations, but the one-off charges and start-up costs were higher, so the underlying performance was actually a bit better than we had foreseen. Growth in the Rest of Europe was especially strong."
"I don't see any reason to change my long-term profit forecasts. On balance, Ahold remains a long-term buy for us."

"The figures came out marginally under my estimate, the main difference coming from operating results, which were a bit below. I had included 12 weeks of Stop and Shop but they consolidated only 11 weeks. If you include the extra week, my operating result (forecast) was still somewhat above the published figures. The main thing is that they had non-recurring provisions at Finast. That was $12 million. I expected $10 million for the full year."
